identity.name: Great Mongol State (Bogd Khanate of Mongolia)
native_names: Богд хаант Монгол Улс (Bogd khaant Mongol Uls)

land.text: Outer Mongolia (Khalkha, Uliastai, Khovd): 'the provisional government issued a proclamation announcing Mongolia's independence' on 1 December 1911

predecessors.note: Uliastai left in December 1911 or January 1912 and Khovd fell only in August 1912 (Mongolian Revolution of 1911 page). The Republic of China inherited the Qing's claim in February 1912.

land.text: the whole of Outer Mongolia: 'MPR proclaimed: 26 November 1924'

successors.note: Cliopatria's Great Mongol State row runs to 1925 and the Mongolian People's Republic row starts in 1926; the 1924-1925 shape is the republic's.

capitals.name: Niislel Khüree (Urga; now Ulaanbaatar)
capitals.note: The Bogd Khanate page names Niislel Khüree as the capital and gives no coordinates (the lon/lat is the gazetteer's Ulaanbaatar). Held by a Chinese garrison November 1919 to February 1921; the provisional revolutionary government sat at Kyakhta Maimaicheng from March 1921 (Revolution of 1921 page).

rulers.name: Bogd Khan (Jebtsundamba Khutuktu)
rulers.title: Bogd Khan
rulers.note: Enthroned 29 December 1911 ('Enthronement of Bogd Khan: 29 December 1911'); the infobox gives his reign as 1911-1919 and 1921-1924. Chinese-guarded figurehead after the November 1919 abolition of autonomy.

rulers.name: Bogd Khan (Jebtsundamba Khutuktu)
rulers.title: Bogd Khan, limited monarch from 11 July 1921
rulers.note: Restored after Ungern-Sternberg took Urga (ceremony 22 February 1921); 'ceremonially installed on the throne of Mongolia' on 11 July 1921 under the people's government; died in 1924. The Bogd page's infobox also lists Roman von Ungern-Sternberg for 1921 as a ruler; not entered as a reign.

union.text: Khovd, the western stronghold of the Qing deputy governor
the Uliastai governorate (Uliastai lies in Dzavhan)

correction.text: Khalkha with Urga, the Provisional Government of Khalkha proclaiming the end of Qing rule on 1 December 1911; the Uliastai and Khovd garrisons still Qing

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for December 1911, the founding month (Cliopatria's row starts in 1912). Outer Mongolia without the two Qing-held western garrisons: the Uliastai governor left only in late December 1911 or January 1912 (sources differ) and Khovd fell in August 1912 ('In August 1912, his stronghold was overcome by Mongolian troops'). The page gives no area; the 1912 outline minus Hovd and Dzavhan is the researcher's reading.

1,569,898 km2 for 1912-1913, the outline of modern Mongolia (the Mongolian People's Republic page gives 1,564,116 km2 with no year; ratio 1.00). The Bogd Khanate page gives no area. It includes Khovd (taken August 1912, ending Qing rule in all of Outer Mongolia) and excludes Tannu Uriankhai (Cliopatria's separate Republic of Uryankhay row, 1912-1913), Inner Mongolia ('Inner Mongolia remains under China') and Barga, whose princes sent statements of support in December 1911 but 'most were too cautious to actually join'.

1,569,528 km2, the same outline (differences from 1912 are 2 cells of 253 km2 on the Tuva frontier, 89.8-92.5E 50.0-50.8N: digitisation noise). Mongolia is an autonomous state under Chinese suzerainty (Sino-Russian Declaration of November 1913; Kyakhta treaty of 1915: 'recognised Mongolia's autonomy within the Chinese state') and Tannu Uriankhai became a Russian protectorate in April 1914, so Tuva stays outside the shape.

1,569,338 km2, the same outline. Chinese troops reach Urga in 1918-1919 and 'Mongolian autonomy was abolished by Chinese authorities in 1919' (17 November 1919, Revolution of 1921 page), so the shape holds for 1917-1919 and the ledger's loss event takes the land from 1920. Cliopatria has no shape for 1920-1921.

correction.text: Mongolia restored after the Chinese garrisons were driven out, the outline of the 1922-1923 shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1921, empty in Cliopatria. Ungern-Sternberg takes Urga in early February 1921 and the Bogd Khan is restored (22 February); the revolutionaries seize the Chinese garrison at Kyakhta Maimaicheng on 18 March; Mongolian and Russian units enter Urga on 6 July and the people's government is proclaimed on 11 July, with the Bogd Khan as limited monarch. The page dates the end of Chinese control only for Urga and Kyakhta; the 1922 outline is used for the whole year.
1,569,338 km2, the same outline as 1917. The state is a limited monarchy under the people's government and 'only recognized by the Russian SFSR' (Bogd page footnote); Tuva (Tannu Tuva) stays outside.

correction.text: unchanged outline; valid for 1924 only, the Mongolian People's Republic from 26 November 1924

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria runs this shape 1924-1925 and the Mongolian People's Republic row begins in 1926, but the Great Mongol State ends with the Bogd Khan's death in 1924 and 'MPR proclaimed: 26 November 1924' (infobox). The outline is right; the years shorten to 1924, and the republic's dossier carries 1924-1925 as its own new keyframe.

union.text: Khovd, the western stronghold of the Qing deputy governor
the Uliastai governorate (Uliastai lies in Dzavhan)

region.text: Khalkha around Urga, without the Uliastai and Khovd garrisons

ledger.note: 1911: Outer Mongolia declares independence from the Qing and the Bogd Khan is enthroned. 'On 1 December 1911, the provisional government issued a proclamation announcing Mongolia's independence'; 'Enthronement of Bogd Khan: 29 December 1911'. The Revolution of 1911 page has the Provisional Government of Khalkha established on 30 November and the Qing amban Sando leaving Urga with a Russian escort on 5 December. The page's name for the state is 'Ikh Mongol uls' (Great Mongol State), 'Bogd Khanate' being a modern label.

region.text: the Uliastai governorate (Uliastai lies in Dzavhan)

ledger.note: January 1912 (or late December 1911): the Qing governor of Uliastai leaves. 'Later that month or in January 1912 (sources differ) the Military Governor of' Uliastai left peacefully under Cossack protection.

region.text: Khovd, the western stronghold of the Qing deputy governor

ledger.note: August 1912: Khovd falls. 'In August 1912, his stronghold was overcome by Mongolian troops'; the Qing deputy governor and staff were escorted out by Cossacks and, the page says, this ended Qing rule in all of Outer Mongolia. The Qing had abdicated in February 1912, so the Republic of China is the legal successor.

region.text: Outer Mongolia, the autonomous territory abolished in 1919

ledger.note: 17 November 1919: China abolishes Mongolian autonomy. 'On 17 November 1919, Xu accepted a petition' for abolishing autonomy (Xu Shuzheng, Northwest Frontier Commissioner since June 1919, entered Urga on 29 October with a military escort); the Bogd page: 'Mongolian autonomy was abolished by Chinese authorities in 1919'. The Bogd page's infobox lists the Republic of China as successor for 1919. The land is held by a Chinese garrison until February 1921, so the loss is recorded rather than an occupation.

February 1921: Ungern-Sternberg takes Urga and restores the Bogd Khan. 'von Ungern-Sternberg launched a second attack in early February 1921' and succeeded; the Bogd Khan and his government were restored 'and a solemn ceremony held on 22 February'. The page gives no day for the Chinese withdrawal, only that it followed the fall of the city (a 7,000-man garrison, besieged since late October 1920).

region.text: Kyakhta Maimaicheng (Altanbulag) on the Mongolian side of the Russian border

ledger.note: 18 March 1921: the revolutionaries take Kyakhta Maimaicheng. A provisional government of seven men was formed on 13 March and 'the guerrilla army seized the garrison' on the 18th, the border trading town opposite Kyakhta.

region.text: Uliastai and Khovd and the rest of Outer Mongolia still under Chinese authority, left after the fall of Urga

ledger.note: February-March 1921: the rest of Outer Mongolia returns to Mongolian rule. 'With the fall of Urga, the Chinese administrations and military garrisons at Uliastai and Khovd departed quickly for Xinjiang' (Urga fell to Ungern-Sternberg in early February 1921); the page gives no day, so the month is bridged to March. Reviewer ia-03-f re-dated this event from July 1921 and raised it from confidence 1 on the page's sentence.

region.text: the whole of Outer Mongolia passes to the republic

ledger.note: 26 November 1924: the Bogd Khan's monarchy gives way to the Mongolian People's Republic. Infobox 'Established: 26 November 1924' (1924 constitution adopted by the first Great Khural); the Bogd Khan died in 1924 (Revolution of 1921 page: 'the death of the Khutuktu in that same year' gave the party its chance).

wars.name: Mongolian Revolution of 1911 (independence from the Qing)

union.text: Khovd, the western stronghold of the Qing deputy governor
the Uliastai governorate (Uliastai lies in Dzavhan)

wars.outcome: The Qing amban left Urga on 5 December 1911, the Uliastai governor in December 1911 or January 1912, and Khovd fell in August 1912, ending Qing rule in all of Outer Mongolia.
wars.note: Not a war of battles: Cossack escorts and negotiated departures except at Khovd. The Qing abdicated in February 1912, so the Republic of China inherited the claim.

wars.name: Mongolian campaign in Inner Mongolia
wars.outcome: 'On 2 February 1913. the Bogd Khanate sent Mongolian cavalry forces to liberate Inner Mongolia from China'; Inner Mongolia stayed under China (Revolution of 1911 page infobox: 'Inner Mongolia remains under China').
wars.note: The Bogd page says nothing of ground taken, so no contest is recorded; the ledger has no gain from this campaign.

wars.name: Chinese reoccupation of Outer Mongolia (Xu Shuzheng)

zones.text: Outer Mongolia, garrisoned by about 7,000 Chinese troops at Urga

wars.outcome: Autonomy abolished 17 November 1919; the Chinese garrison at Urga held until Ungern-Sternberg's attack of early February 1921.

wars.name: Ungern-Sternberg's Mongolian campaign
belligerents: Asiatic Cavalry Division of Roman von Ungern-Sternberg
wars.outcome: About 1,000 men besieged the Chinese garrison in late October-early November 1920 and were repulsed; the second attack in early February 1921 took Urga and the Bogd Khan was restored on 22 February.

wars.name: Mongolian Revolution of 1921
wars.outcome: The Chinese garrison at Kyakhta Maimaicheng fell on 18 March 1921; Mongolian and Russian units entered Urga on 6 July and the people's government was proclaimed on 11 July with the Bogd Khan as limited monarch.
wars.note: Soviet main corps crossed the border on 28 June 1921; the page does not date a Soviet withdrawal.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is dated for Outer Mongolia on any page opened; the frontier with Inner Mongolia and Barga was a claim that failed (1913), the Tuva frontier moved with the Russian protectorate (April 1914), and the Russian frontier follows older treaty lines that were not opened. The 1915 Kyakhta treaty fixed a status, not a boundary.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Great Mongol State' row (1912-1925) is the Bogd Khanate of Mongolia, not the Yuan dynasty: its Wikipedia field says 'Yuan dynasty' and its Wikidata id Q7313 is shared with great-yuan and yuan-dynasty, which are different states (the Yuan 1271-1368). 'Ikh Mongol Uls' (Great Mongol State) is the Bogd Khanate's own official name, so the Cliopatria label is right and the link is wrong; wikidata is set to null here because the right id could not be read from a page. The row runs to 1925 but the state ends on 26 November 1924 and the republic that follows is the mongolian-people-s-republic dossier (Cliopatria row from 1926). Cliopatria has no shape for 1920-1921: a new keyframe is added for 1921 only (the state held no land in 1920; reviewer ia-03-f removed a 1920 keyframe that drew the Chinese-held outline under this state); the Chinese rule of 17 November 1919 to February 1921 is recorded as loss/gain with republic-of-china (the Bogd page's infobox lists the Republic of China as successor for 1919); the Kuomintang 1920-1921 shape does not include Mongolia, so the ea-08 dossiers need the mirror events (ROC gain November 1919, loss February-March 1921). Relations the other dossiers should carry: the Republic of China held Outer Mongolia as an autonomous territory under Chinese suzerainty from the Sino-Russian Declaration of November 1913 (Bogd page) / Kyakhta treaty of May-June 1915 until November 1919 (vassal_start/vassal_end with counterpart great-mongol-state); the Russian Empire had a protectorate over Tannu Uriankhai from April 1914 (see republic-of-uryankhay). Not settled: Barga/Hulunbuir (the Bogd page mentions it only in an undated list), the 1912 Russian-Mongolian agreement ('At the end of 1912', no day), the exact dates of the Kyakhta treaty (25 May, 29 May and 17 June 1915 on three pages), Altai/Dorbet areas, and the date the Chinese left the western provinces in 1921. Ungern-Sternberg's regime (February-August 1921) is treated as part of the same state because he restored the Bogd Khan; the people's government sat at Kyakhta Maimaicheng from March 1921.
